definition: a common yellow-flowered weed with jagged leaves and windborne seeds
hook: Dandelion is named after a lion's teeth, not its flower.
modernAnchor: We blow its seeds into the wind and never once picture a lion's mouth.
journey: Medieval French herbalists looked at the plant's jagged, pointed leaves and saw something else entirely.
The leaves reminded them of a lion's sharp teeth, so they named the plant dent de lion.
English speakers borrowed the French phrase and mashed its three words into one, dandelion.
The lion's teeth stayed hidden in the spelling long after everyone stopped picturing an actual lion.
